title: Codable: JSON in and out, with the compiler doing the work

videos.script: A planner has to remember. Its courses and sessions go to a file, or to a server, and come back. {{encode}} In Swift, one word does the work. Mark a struct Codable, and the compiler writes the code that turns it into JSON. You will write a planner to a file, and see the same program put its keys in a different order on each run. {{decode}} Then back again. The type you ask for is the whole specification, checked value by value. {{keys}} Then a server that names its fields its own way, and the small enum that maps one set of names to the other. {{dates}} Then dates, where the default is a number almost nobody expects. {{missing}} Then keys that are missing, and where a default belongs. {{errors}} And last, the errors themselves. Which case went wrong, and the path to the exact record that broke.
